reflection.text:
High-dose acquisition at 3 uM (e2) immediately showed the decisive stabilizer signature: very high tub_glcm_contrast z=+121.7, tub_std z=+69.7 with lower cell counts, replicated at 0.1, 0.3 and 1 uM with tub_mean up to +58.7 and contrast up to +154.7 (e3, e7, e8). Visual bundling on describe_phenotype (e4) plus unanimous 4/4 NSC vote for Microtubule stabilizers (e5, e9) correctly ruled out destabilizers which would dim tubulin, consistent with epothilone B as a microtubule-stabilizer (PMID 41663006) that suppresses dynamics and causes mitotic arrest (PMID 14522931).

The main ambiguity was in the k-neighbour distributions: 3/10 Eg5 inhibitors in the first comparison (e5) and 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers in the second (e9), likely driven by shared mitotic nuclear shape change nuc_solidity z=-39.8 and reduced density rather than tubulin brightness. I correctly down-weighted these because tub_mean/std/contrast were bright, not dim, and the per-well 1-NN similarities to stabilizers were high at 0.63-0.896.

The acquisition choice to sample four contiguous mid-high doses established dose continuity but skipped the lowest doses and second replicates, so potency threshold and technical reproducibility were not directly tested. Unblinding to epothilone B with ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser confirmed the call.
what_was_right: Prioritized high-dose 3 uM well (e2) then 0.1 uM (e3) which revealed bright tubulin signal tub_mean +18.3 to +58.7, tub_std +33.1 to +87.2, tub_glcm_contrast +28.0 to +154.7 across all 4 wells, opposite of destabilizer dimming.
Used describe_phenotype (e4) visual thick bundles plus lower density to link texture metrics to stabilizer bundling and mitotic arrest rather than actin or Eg5 morphology.
Required replication at 0.3 uM (e7) and 1 uM (e8) and final 4/4 NSC vote with high similarities 0.63, 0.894, 0.862, 0.896 (verdict protocol) before submitting at p=0.96.
what_was_wrong: Initial k-neighbours included Eg5 inhibitors 3/10 and Actin disruptors 1/10 (e5); I retained Eg5 at 0.05 hypotheses in step 6 and did not explicitly test nuclear monopolar versus bundled-tubulin distinction.
Second atlas comparison (e9) showed Microtubule destabilizers 3/10 neighbours, which I noted but did not resolve mechanistically beyond bright-versus-dim tubulin reasoning.

Acquisition plan used only rep 1 wells at 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 3 uM and only 2 fields for microscopy, missing low-dose baseline and replicate wells that would have strengthened potency and reproducibility evidence.

citations.claim: Epothilone B is explicitly annotated as a microtubule-stabilizer, supporting the stabilizer call.
Epothilone B suppresses microtubule dynamics and is associated with mitotic arrest, linking bundling to lower density.
Epothilone B promotes microtubule stabilization, consistent with increased tubulin intensity and texture.

# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_f3007822f1

Run `run_d55b09e6a606` · blinded · 2026-10-31 19:47 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e2 | 3 | 1 | 137 | tub_glcm_contrast z=+121.7; tub_std z=+69.7; nuc_solidity z=-39.8 |

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Microtubule stabilizers 0.88, Eg5 inhibitors 0.05, Microtubule destabilizers 0.04, Actin disruptors 0.03
- after step 10: Microtubule stabilizers 0.96, Microtubule destabilizers 0.02, Eg5 inhibitors 0.01, Actin disruptors 0.01

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.96); key evidence e2, e4, e7, e8, e9.

Why: Replicated bright bundled tubulin signature and unanimous 4/4 atlas vote support stabilizer MoA.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Live-cell tubulin polymerization assay with washout plus phospho-histone H3 mitotic index to confirm stabilized microtubules and mitotic arrest.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean win for the tubulin-bright phenotype: many-fold-higher tub mean with huge std/contrast in all 4 wells (z_mean up to +59, z_std to +87, z_contrast +28-155) plus visual thick bundles shows a stabilizer; destabilizers would dim/fragment tubulin, actin disruptors and Eg5 inhibitors would not brighten tubulin, and Aurora/mitosis blockers would score low on bright bundled tubulin. The 4/4 atlas result confirms this was not a single-dose artifact (P(y_true=PS|E) says the observed cell state is real; only a clean KMS002 negative pair controls it).

## Unblinding

Compound: **epothilone B** (PubChem CID [448013](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/448013))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin stabiliser

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule stabilizers**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Microtubule stabilizers** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

High-dose acquisition at 3 uM (e2) immediately showed the decisive stabilizer signature: very high tub_glcm_contrast z=+121.7, tub_std z=+69.7 with lower cell counts, replicated at 0.1, 0.3 and 1 uM with tub_mean up to +58.7 and contrast up to +154.7 (e3, e7, e8). Visual bundling on describe_phenotype (e4) plus unanimous 4/4 NSC vote for Microtubule stabilizers (e5, e9) correctly ruled out destabilizers which would dim tubulin, consistent with epothilone B as a microtubule-stabilizer (PMID 41663006) that suppresses dynamics and causes mitotic arrest (PMID 14522931).

The main ambiguity was in the k-neighbour distributions: 3/10 Eg5 inhibitors in the first comparison (e5) and 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers in the second (e9), likely driven by shared mitotic nuclear shape change nuc_solidity z=-39.8 and reduced density rather than tubulin brightness. I correctly down-weighted these because tub_mean/std/contrast were bright, not dim, and the per-well 1-NN similarities to stabilizers were high at 0.63-0.896.

The acquisition choice to sample four contiguous mid-high doses established dose continuity but skipped the lowest doses and second replicates, so potency threshold and technical reproducibility were not directly tested. Unblinding to epothilone B with ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser confirmed the call.

What was right:
- Prioritized high-dose 3 uM well (e2) then 0.1 uM (e3) which revealed bright tubulin signal tub_mean +18.3 to +58.7, tub_std +33.1 to +87.2, tub_glcm_contrast +28.0 to +154.7 across all 4 wells, opposite of destabilizer dimming.
- Used describe_phenotype (e4) visual thick bundles plus lower density to link texture metrics to stabilizer bundling and mitotic arrest rather than actin or Eg5 morphology.
- Required replication at 0.3 uM (e7) and 1 uM (e8) and final 4/4 NSC vote with high similarities 0.63, 0.894, 0.862, 0.896 (verdict protocol) before submitting at p=0.96.

What was wrong or missed:
- Initial k-neighbours included Eg5 inhibitors 3/10 and Actin disruptors 1/10 (e5); I retained Eg5 at 0.05 hypotheses in step 6 and did not explicitly test nuclear monopolar versus bundled-tubulin distinction.
- Second atlas comparison (e9) showed Microtubule destabilizers 3/10 neighbours, which I noted but did not resolve mechanistically beyond bright-versus-dim tubulin reasoning.
- Acquisition plan used only rep 1 wells at 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 3 uM and only 2 fields for microscopy, missing low-dose baseline and replicate wells that would have strengthened potency and reproducibility evidence.

Proposed next experiment: Live-cell tubulin polymerization assay with washout plus phospho-histone H3 mitotic index and DNA content to confirm persistent stabilized bundles and mitotic arrest versus Eg5 inhibitor monopolar phenotype.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [41663006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41663006/): Microtubule-stabilizer epothilone B counteracts anesthetic-induced slowed swimming in Tetrahymena pyriformis. *Exp Cell Res* (2026) — Epothilone B is explicitly annotated as a microtubule-stabilizer, supporting the stabilizer call.
- PMID [14522931](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14522931/): Suppression of microtubule dynamics by epothilone B is associated with mitotic arrest. *Cancer Res* (2003) — Epothilone B suppresses microtubule dynamics and is associated with mitotic arrest, linking bundling to lower density.
- PMID [29348323](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29348323/): Epothilone B Benefits Nigrostriatal Pathway Recovery by Promoting Microtubule Stabilization After Intracerebral Hemorrhage. *J Am Heart Assoc* (2018) — Epothilone B promotes microtubule stabilization, consistent with increased tubulin intensity and texture.
